subject: Banking
title: The European Central Bank
description: A fast breakdown of The European Central Bank for builders.

hook.text: The ECB sets monetary policy for 20 countries using one currency.

buildup.text: Created in 1998, the ECB manages the euro. Its primary mandate is price stability, targeting inflation near 2%.

discovery.text: The ECB's Governing Council has 26 members: 6 Executive Board members and 20 national central bank governors.

twist.text: What's right for Germany's economy is often wrong for Greece's.

climax.text: The ECB manages a monetary union without a fiscal union. One currency, 20 budgets, and no easy way to reconcile them.

punchline.text: One rate for 20 economies. The ECB manages an impossible compromise.

quiz.question: How many countries does the ECB set monetary policy for?

details.summary: The European Central Bank manages monetary policy for 20 eurozone countries with vastly different economies, creating a permanent tension between the one-size-fits-all rate needed for the euro and the diverse needs of member states.
details.whyItMatters: The ECB's challenge of setting a single interest rate for economies as different as Germany and Greece reveals the fundamental trade-offs of shared currency. Its decisions affect 350 million people and the global economy.
takeaways: The ECB sets one interest rate for 20 countries with different economic conditions
Germany and southern Europe often need opposite monetary policies
The ECB is prohibited from directly financing member state governments

faq.question: Why is one interest rate for all eurozone countries problematic?
faq.answer: Germany might need high rates to cool inflation while Greece needs low rates to stimulate growth. The ECB must choose one rate, inevitably too loose for some members and too tight for others, creating recurring tensions.

faq.question: How powerful is the ECB compared to the Fed?
faq.answer: The ECB controls monetary policy for the world's second-largest currency area but lacks the Fed's dual mandate for employment. It also operates under stricter legal constraints, particularly the prohibition on monetary financing of governments.
